questions.q: What does fork testing let you do that a fresh, empty test deployment can't?
options: Run tests faster
Test your contract's interactions with real external state — real Uniswap pools, real Chainlink feeds, real token behavior
Skip writing assertions entirely
Avoid needing an RPC provider
questions.explain: A fresh deployment has none of mainnet's real liquidity, price feeds, or token quirks — fork testing runs against an actual copy of that state.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend pinning `--fork-block-number` instead of forking "latest"?
options: It's required by Foundry and can't be omitted
It makes the test reproducible — the same real-world state every run, instead of whatever mainnet looks like right now
It makes tests run without an internet connection
It disables gas metering
questions.explain: Pinning a block number means every test run sees identical state, which is essential for debugging a failure reliably later.

questions.q: What do `vm.createFork` and `vm.selectFork` let a single test do?
options: Deploy the same contract to two chains simultaneously
Hold multiple forks and switch which chain's state subsequent calls in the test actually see
Automatically bridge tokens between chains
Merge two forks into one
questions.explain: createFork sets up a fork; selectFork switches the active one, letting a test check state on, say, both sides of a bridge in one function.

questions.q: Where does Forge cache fetched fork state when both --fork-url and --fork-block-number are specified?
options: It never caches — every run re-fetches from the RPC
In the project's .git directory
Locally at ~/.foundry/cache/rpc/<chain>/<block>/
In a cloud database managed by Foundry
questions.explain: Forge caches fetched RPC state locally keyed by chain and block, so repeated runs read from disk instead of hitting the RPC provider again.

options: Slow compilation times
RPC provider rate limiting, by adding exponential backoff to fork requests
Gas price volatility during a test
Out-of-order test execution
questions.explain: If an RPC provider starts rate-limiting fork requests, --fork-retry-backoff adds exponential backoff instead of letting the test suite fail outright.
